bmt-2022-algebra-tiebreaker-02.title: Polar form and conjugate roots
bmt-2022-algebra-tiebreaker-02.body:
$i-1=\sqrt2\,(\cos\tfrac{3\pi}4+i\sin\tfrac{3\pi}4)$, so $(i-1)^{11}=2^{11/2}\left(\cos\tfrac{33\pi}4+i\sin\tfrac{33\pi}4\right)=2^{11/2}\left(\cos\tfrac\pi4+i\sin\tfrac\pi4\right)=32+32i$.

Since $A,B$ are real, the conjugate $32-32i$ is also a root. By Vieta, $A=-64$ and $B=32^2+32^2=2048$, so $A+B=1984$.

**Answer: 1984**

bmt-2022-algebra-tiebreaker-03.title: Find an invariant
bmt-2022-algebra-tiebreaker-03.body:
Let $b=\left(1-\frac1a\right)^{-1}$ for each number $a$ on the board. For the new number $w=\frac{xy}{x+y-1}$ we get $\frac1w=\frac1x+\frac1y-\frac1{xy}$, so $1-\frac1w=\left(1-\frac1x\right)\left(1-\frac1y\right)$.

Thus the product of all the quantities $1-\frac1a$ on the board never changes. Initially it is $\prod_{a=2}^{101}\frac{a-1}a=\frac12\cdot\frac23\cdots\frac{100}{101}=\frac{1}{101}$. The final number $F$ satisfies $1-\frac1F=\frac1{101}$, so $F=\frac{101}{100}$. It does not depend on the order, so this is the only (hence maximum) value.

**Answer: $\frac{101}{100}$**
